NORTHERN PROVINCE PROVINCIAL COUNCIL
Northern Province Provincial Council Health Services Statute No. 01 of 2015

NOTICE is hereby given that the Northern Province, Provincial Council has adopted the Northern Province Health ServicesStatute No. 01 of 2015 on 12th January 2016 and that the Hon. Governor, Northern Province has granted his Assent to iton 08.02.2016
K. THEIVENDRAN,
Secretary,Council Secretariat,Northern Provincial Council.
Council Secretariat,A9 Road,Kaithady,19th February 2016.
THE HEALTH SERVICES STATUTE

A Statute to provide for the establishment of a Northern Province Department of Health Services,to provide for the continuation of services for the promotion and preservation of the health of thepeople in the Northern Province ; and to provide for all the matters connected therewith and incidentalthereto.
This Statute is inconsistent with the Health Service Act, No. 12 of 1952 as amended.
Be it enacted by the Provincial Council of the Northern Province as follows :-
1. This Statute may be cited as the Northern Province Health Services Statute, No. 1 of 2015, and
shall come into force on the date on which is receives the assent of the Governor.

PART I
ESTABLISHMENT OF THE NORTHERN PROVINCE DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH SERVICES, ITS
CONSTITUTION AND RESPONSIBILITIES
2(1) There shall be a Northern Province Department of Health Services (hereinafter referred to
as “the Department”) which shall be administered in accordance with the provisions of thisStatute.
(2) The appointment, transfer, dismissal and disciplinary control of officers of the Department
(other than officers in an All-island Service seconded for service in the Department) shallvest in the Governor in terms of Part IV of the Provincial Councils Act, No. 42 of 1987.
3 The functions of the Department shall be -
a) to establish, administer and maintain Health institutions set out hereinafter in the Schedule
to this Statute, and to promote the improvement of the services provided by them ;
b) to establish and maintain institutions set out hereinafter in the Schedule to this Statute as

required for the provision of services relating to public health, educating the public onhealth issues, nutrition, family health maternity and child care, food and food sanitationand enviornmental health ;
c) to implement the Provincial Health Development Plan and the Annual Health Plan for the
Province ;
d) to provide all facilities (other than drugs) to the hospitals and institutions referred to in
sub-paragraphs (a) and (b) ;
e) to identify the staff and other servants required for the efficient discharge of services to be
provided by the hospitals institutions referred to in sub-paragraphs (a) and (b) and to makerecommendations in respect of such requirements to the relevant authorities ;
f) to provide capacity improvement programmes for all categories of staff of the Department
; and
g) generally to do all such other things as are necessary to facilitate the proper discharge of
the functions of the Department.
41. There shall be a Provincial Dircector of Health Services (hereinafter referred to as “the

Provincial Director”) who shall be the head of the Northern Province Department of HealthServices and shall, subject to the direction and supervision of the Secretary, implement theprovisions of this Statute.
2. There shall be appointed a Deputy Provincial Director of Health Services (hereinafter

referred to as “the Deputy Provincial Director - Health Services”) and a Deputy ProvincialDirector of Administration (hereinafter referred to as “the Deputy Provincial Director -Administration”), who shall assist the Provincial Director in the discharge of his functions,duties and responsibilities.
51. There shall be five Regional Directors of Health Services appointed respectively, for the
districts of Jaffna, Kilinochchi, Mullaitivu, Vavuniya and Mannar.

2. Subject of the direction and supervision of the Provincial Director, the Regional Directors
of Health Services shall be responsible for the provision of health services in theirrespective districts.
61. The Provincial Director shall facilities the preparation of the Annual Health Plan for the
succeeding year, taking into consideration the following in respect of the Province.
a) the increase of population in relation to the extent of land ;b) the spread of disease ;
c) the nutritional condition of the people ;d) the impact of the environment on health ; and
e) transport facilities available.
The Plan shall give a description of the development and construction activities proposedto be undertaken during the succeeding year.
2. The Provincial Director shall submit the Annual Health Plan to the Secretary who shall

then place it before the Provincial Health Services Advisory Board for its observations,The Secretary shall consider incorporating any observations of the Provincial HealthServices Advisory Board which in his opinion facilitate the provision of health services inthe Province and approve the Plan, before the thirtieth day of November of the year precedingthe year to which the Annual Health Plan relates. Then the Secretary will submit the AnnualHealth Plan to the Board of Ministers through the Minister of Health for the approval ofthe Board of Ministers.
3. Any development or construction activity which is not referred to in the Annual health Plan
for a particular year shall not be undertaken in that year, except with the approval of theBoard of Ministers.
7 The Provincial Director shall submit to the Secretary, before the end of the first quarter of every

year, a report with regard to the state of public health in the Province in the preceding year. Thereport shall identify, with statistics, the successes and the weaknesses in implementing the AnnualHealth Development Plan during the preceding year, and recommend measures to correct anyweakness identified.
8 The Provincial Director may, by notice in writing, request the Secretary or the Commissioner, as

the case may be, of any local authority in the Northern Province to provide necessary particularsand information with regard to health conditions within the respective administrative limits. TheSecretary or Commissioner, as the case may be, shall assist the Provincial Director by providingthe relevant information.
91. The Minister may make regulations in respect of any matter required by this Statute to be
prescribed or in respect of which regulations are authorized or required by this Statute tobe made.
2. Every regulation made under this section shall be published in the Gazette and shall come
into operation on the date of such publication or on such later date as may be specified insuch regulation.
3. Every regulation made by the Minister shall, before the expiration of one month after its

publication in the Gazette, be brought before the Provincial Council for its approval, Everyregulation which is not so approved shall be deemed to be rescinded as from the date ofsuch disapproval but without prejudice to anything previously done there under. Notificationof the date on which any regulation is deemed to be rescineded shall be published in theGazette.

PART II
PROVINCIAL HEALTH SERVICES ADVISORY BOARD AND HOSPITAL DEVELOPMENT
COMMITTEE
101. There shall be established a Provincial Health Services Advisory Board (hereinafter referred
to as “the Advisory Board”)
2. The Advisory Board shall be appointed by the Minister and shall consist of not more than
Nineteen (19) members appointed in the following manner.
a. ex-officio members, namely -
i. the Provincial Director of Health Services ;ii. the Provincial Director of Education ;iii. the Provincial Commissioner of Local Government ;
iv. the Provincial Director of Social Services ;
v. the Provincial Commissioner of Indigenous Medicine ;vi. every Regional Director of Health Services in-charge of a district ; andb. the following members who shall be known as “appointed members” -
i. four members from amongst medical practitioners working in the hospitals
and institutions referred to in sub-paragraphs (a) and (b) of Section 3, andspecializing respectively, in Community Medicine, General Medicine,Obstetrics and Paediatrics ;
ii. five members from amongst persons with at least ten (10) years of experience
in the filds of Health and Social Services to represent Jaffna, Kilinochchi,Mullaitivu, Vanuniya and Mannar districts respectively
3. No person shall be qualified to be appointed or continue as a member of the Advisory
Board if -
a) he is not a citizen of Sri Lanka ;b) he has not attained the age of eighteen years ;
c) he is or becomes a Member of Parliament, any Provincial Council or any Local
Authority ;d) he has been declared an undischarged bankrupt or insolvent under any law in force in
Sri Lanka or any other country.e) he is under any law in force in Sri Lanka or any other country found or declared to be
of unsound mind ;f) he is convicted of any offence involving moral turpitude or punishable with
imprisonment for a term not less than six months.g) he is serving or has served a sentence of imprisonment imposed by a court of law in
Sri Lanka or any other country ; orh) he has any financial or other interest as is likely to affect the discharge of his functions
as a member of the Advisory Board.
4. The Provincial Director shall be the Chairman of the Advisory Board and the Secretary of
the Advisory Board shall be elected from amongst the ex-officio members of the AdvisoryBoard.
5. The terms of office of every ex-officio member shall be the period during which he holds
the post by virtue of which he is a member of the Advisory Board.

6. Each members has rights to cast one vote. in case of tie, the Chairman has the right
to exercise his casting vote.
7. An appointed member may resign from office by letter addressed to the Minister.
8. The Minister may, for reasons assigned, remove and appointed member from office.
9. Subject to sub-sections (7) and (8), the term of office of an appointed member shall be
two years.
10. An appointed member, who ceases to hold office by effluxion of time, shall be eligible for
reappointment.
11. Where an appointed member vacates, office by resignation, death, removal by the Minister

or otherwise, the Minister shall, having regard to the provisions of sub-paragraph (b) ofsub-section 2, appoint another person to fill such vacancy. The person so appointed shallhold office for the unexpired period of the term of office of the member whom he succeeds.
12. The Advisory Board shall meet at least once in three months or whenever necessary.
13. The Secretary shall summon meetings of the Advisory Board, and shall maintain minutes
of the meetings of Advisory Board.
14. The quorum for a meeting of the Advisory Board shall be eleven (11), including the
Chairman.
15. Members who attend meetings of the Advisory Board shall be paid allowances of such
amount as may be determined by the Minister in consultation with the Minister in-chargeof the subject of Finance and with the concurrence of the Governor.
11 The functions of the Advisory Board shall be to make recommendations and observations to the

Minister on matters referred to it by the Minister for the planning and provision of health servicesin the Province, the improvement of the services provided by the Department and generally, forthe promotion and preservation of the health of the people in the Province.
121. The Secretary shall, with the approval of the Minister, appoint for every hospital and
institution set out in sub-paragraphs (a) and (b) of section 3 a Development Committee forthe development of such institution.
2. Every Development Committee appointed, under sub-section (1) shall consist of -
a) ex-officio members, namely -

i. the Medical Officer in-charge of that hospital or institutions ;ii. the Divisional Secretary of the Division within which that institution is situated ;iii. A representative of the Buildings Department not below the rank of Techincal
Officer ;iv. the Secretary or Commissioner, as the case may be, of every local autority
within the administrative limits of which that insitution is situated ; and

3. No person shall be qualfied to be appointed or continue as a member of a Development
Committee if -
a) he is not a citizen of Sri Lanka ;b) he has not attained the age of eighteen years ;
c) he is or becomes a Member of Parliament, any Provincial Council or any Local
Authority ;d) he has been declared an undischarged bankrupt or insolvent under any law in force in
Sri Lanka or any other country ;e) he is under any law in force in Sri Lanka or any other country found or declared to be
of unsound mind ;f) he is convicted of any offence involving moral turpitude or punishment with
imprisonment for a term not less than six months.g) he is serving or has served a sentence of imprisonment imposed by a court of law in
Sri Lanka or any other country ; orh) he has any financial or other interest as it likely to affect the discharge or his functions
as a member of the Advisory Board.
4. The term of office of every ex-officio member shall be the period during which he holds
the post by virtue of which he is a member of the Committee.
5. Each member has rights to cast one vote. In case of tie, the Chairman has the right to
excercise his casting vote.
6. An appointed member may resign from office by letter addressed to the Secretary.
7. The Secretary may, for reasons assigned and subject to the approval of the Minister, remove
an appointed member from office.
8. Subject to sub-sections (6) and (7), the term of office of an appointed member shall be
two years.
9. An appointed member, who ceases to hold office by effluxion of time, shall be eligible for
reappointment.
10. Where an appointed member vacates office by resignation, death, removal by the Secretary

or otherwise, the Secretary shall, having regard to the provisons of sub-paragraph (b) ofsub-section 2, appoint another person to fill such vacancy. The person so appointed shallhold office for the unexpired period of the term of office of the member whom he succeeds.
11. The Medical Officer referred to in sub-paragraph (a) of sub-section 2 shall be the Chairman

of the Development Committee appointed for that institution. A person elected by themembers shall be the Secretary of the Development Committee. The Secretary shall maintainminutes of the meetings of the Committee.

12. Every Development Committee appointed for a particular institution may, subject to the
approval of the Secretary, take measures for the development and rehabilitation of thatinstitution.
13. A Development Committee appointed for a Hospital prior to the coming into force of this

Statute shall, for all purposes, be deemed to be a Committee appointed under this Statute.Members of such Committee shall continue to hold office as members of a HospitalDevelopment Committee appointed in accordance with the provisions of this Statute untila new committee is appointed in accordance with the provisons of sub-section 1.
PART III - GENERAL
13. Subject to the national policy on health, all services provided in the Hospitals and institutions
referred to in sub-paragraphs (a) and (b) of section 3 shall be provided without any charge.
14 In case of any inconsistency between the Tamil and the Sinhala or Engilsh text of this statute, the
Tamil text shall prevail.
15 In this Statute unless the context otherwise requires -
“Department” means the Northern Province Department of Health Services ;
“Local authority” means a Municipal Council, Urban Council or Pradeshiya Sabha in the Northern Province ;
“Governor” means the Governor of the Northern Province ;
“Medical practitioner” means a person registered as a medical practitioner under the Medical Ordinance.
“Minister” means the Minister of the Board of Ministers of the Northern Province, in-charge of the
subject of health ;
“Province” means the Northern Province consisting of the administrative District of Jaffna, Kilinochchi,
Mannar, Vanuniya and Mullaitivu ;
“Provincial Director of Health Services” means the Director of the Northern Province Department of
Health Services ;
“Secretary” means the Secretary to the Ministry of the Minister of the Board of Ministers of the Northern
Province, in-charge of the subject of health.
